Simulate parameter recovery by repeated generation and refitting

Source: R/api-simulation.R
simulate_mfrm_recovery.Rd

Runs a compact parameter-recovery simulation study: generate data from a known ordered many-facet data-generating setup, refit the requested model, align estimates to the known truth where location indeterminacy requires it, and summarize bias, RMSE, MAE, correlation, and coverage of available centered structural facet intervals. This function runs the simulation and fits models. To review an already saved simulation result without new data generation or fitting, use assess_mfrm_recovery(). In 0.2.4 this replaces evaluate_mfrm_recovery(); the old name remains an alias. See the details for corrected recovery targets, Monte Carlo uncertainty and migration of saved results.

Usage

simulate_mfrm_recovery(
  n_person = 50,
  n_rater = 4,
  n_criterion = 4,
  raters_per_person = n_rater,
  design = NULL,
  reps = 10,
  score_levels = 4,
  theta_sd = 1,
  rater_sd = 0.35,
  criterion_sd = 0.25,
  noise_sd = 0,
  step_span = 1.4,
  model = c("RSM", "PCM", "GPCM"),
  step_facet = NULL,
  slope_facet = NULL,
  thresholds = NULL,
  slopes = NULL,
  assignment = NULL,
  sparse_controls = NULL,
  sim_spec = NULL,
  fit_method = c("JML", "MML"),
  maxit = 25,
  quad_points = 7,
  include_person = TRUE,
  include_diagnostics = FALSE,
  diagnostic_fit_df_method = c("both", "engine", "facets"),
  seed = NULL,
  file = NULL,
  file_refit = c("never", "on_change", "always")
)

Arguments

n_person

Number of persons/respondents.

n_rater

Number of rater facet levels.

n_criterion

Number of criterion/item facet levels.

raters_per_person

Number of raters assigned to each person.

design

Optional named design override supplied as a named list, named vector, or one-row data frame. When sim_spec = NULL, names may use canonical variables (n_person, n_rater, n_criterion, raters_per_person) or role keywords (person, rater, criterion, assignment). A nested named-facet form, design$facets = c(person = ..., rater = ..., criterion = ...), is also accepted for the supported person/rater/criterion design. Do not specify the same variable through both design and the scalar count arguments.

reps

Number of Monte Carlo replications.

score_levels

Number of ordered score categories.

theta_sd

Standard deviation of simulated person measures.

rater_sd

Standard deviation of simulated rater severities.

criterion_sd

Standard deviation of simulated criterion difficulties.

noise_sd

Optional observation-level noise added to the linear predictor.

step_span

Spread of step thresholds on the logit scale.

model

Measurement model recorded in the simulation setup. The current public generator supports RSM, PCM, and GPCM.

step_facet

Step facet used when model = "PCM" and threshold values vary across levels. Currently "Criterion" and "Rater" are supported.

slope_facet

Slope facet used when model = "GPCM". The current GPCM branch requires slope_facet == step_facet.

thresholds

Optional threshold specification. Use a numeric vector of common thresholds; a named list such as list(C01 = c(-1, 0, 1)); a numeric matrix with one row per StepFacet and one column per step; or a long data frame with columns StepFacet, Step/StepIndex, and Estimate.

slopes

Optional slope specification used when model = "GPCM". Use either a numeric vector aligned to the generated slope-facet levels or a data frame with columns SlopeFacet and Estimate. Supplied slopes are treated as relative discriminations and normalized to the package's geometric-mean-one identification convention on the log scale. When omitted, slopes default to 1 for every slope-facet level, giving an exact PCM reduction.

assignment

Assignment design. "crossed" means every person sees every rater; "rotating" uses a balanced rotating subset; "resampled" reuses person-level rater-assignment profiles stored in sim_spec; "sparse_linked" uses an incomplete rating design with optional linking persons; "skeleton" reuses an observed response skeleton stored in sim_spec, including optional Group/Weight columns when available. When omitted, the function chooses "crossed" if raters_per_person == n_rater, otherwise "rotating".

sparse_controls

Optional named list used when assignment = "sparse_linked". Supported entries are link_fraction, link_persons, link_raters_per_person, assignment_mode, and min_common_persons_per_rater_pair. See build_mfrm_sim_spec() for the same contract.

sim_spec

Optional output from build_mfrm_sim_spec() or extract_mfrm_sim_spec(). When supplied, it defines the generator setup; direct scalar arguments are treated as legacy inputs and should generally be left at their defaults except for seed. Any custom public two-facet names recorded in sim_spec$facet_names are also carried into the simulated output and downstream planning helpers. If sim_spec stores an active latent-regression population generator, the returned object also carries the generated one-row-per-person background-data table needed to refit that population model later.

fit_method

"JML" or "MML", passed to fit_mfrm().

maxit

Maximum optimizer iterations passed to fit_mfrm().

quad_points

Quadrature points used when fit_method = "MML".

include_person

Logical. When TRUE, include person-measure recovery rows when the fitted object exposes person estimates.

include_diagnostics

Logical. When TRUE, run diagnose_mfrm() after each successful refit and retain facet-level fit/separation operating characteristics. These diagnostics are reported separately from recovery metrics and are not parameter-recovery criteria by themselves.

diagnostic_fit_df_method

Fit-ZSTD degrees-of-freedom convention used for optional diagnostic operating-characteristic summaries. Use "both" when reviewing FACETS-style df sensitivity.

seed

Optional random seed.

file

Optional RDS path for saving and reusing the simulation. A missing .rds extension is appended. Its parent directory must already exist. NULL (default) performs no file reads or writes.

file_refit

File reuse policy. "never" (default) loads a matching completed result or resumes matching saved trials; incompatible files produce an error. "on_change" restarts when inputs or implementation/ environment differ. "always" replaces the file with a new run. Unlike brms::brm(file_refit = "never"), this function checks compatibility even under "never"; it does not silently return a different analysis.

Value

An object of class mfrm_recovery_simulation with components:

  • recovery: row-level truth/estimate comparisons and interval availability by replication.

  • recovery_summary: parameter-group metrics, trial MCSEs, denominators, availability rates and interval reasons.

  • recovery_targets: target counts by replication and parameter group, recorded before fitting.

  • rep_overview: replication-level convergence, timing, error status, and sparse-design diagnostics when applicable.

  • diagnostic_oc: optional replication-by-facet fit/separation operating characteristics when include_diagnostics = TRUE.

  • diagnostic_oc_summary: optional facet-level diagnostic operating- characteristic summary.

  • settings: fitting and simulation settings.

  • ademp: simulation-study metadata.

  • reproducibility: file identity, original inputs and per-trial seeds when file is supplied.

Details

This helper is deliberately narrower than evaluate_mfrm_design(). Design evaluation asks which design condition is operationally adequate; recovery simulation asks whether the fitted model recovers the known parameters under one explicit data-generating setup.

Location-like parameters (Person, non-person facets, and steps) are summarized after mean alignment within each replication and parameter group. These errors describe relative locations within the matched group. Their average Bias is zero by construction, so it cannot establish absence of bias for individual parameters. BiasBasis identifies this restriction; assess_mfrm_recovery() leaves its bias check not_assessed. Inspect RMSE and row-level errors for relative recovery instead.

PCM/GPCM step vectors are centered within their owning facet level. Their generating step means are therefore added to the corresponding facet truth before comparison. A generated population intercept, when fitted, is shifted consistently with the fitted facet/step identification. RawTruth retains the original generator parameter. Truth is the comparison-coordinate truth; ErrorRaw, RawBias and RawRMSE use this truth before the additional within-group mean alignment, not necessarily RawTruth.

For GPCM, supplied generator slopes are treated as relative discriminations and normalized to the same geometric-mean-one log-slope identification used by the fitter. Slope recovery is therefore summarized on the identified log-slope scale without an additional mean-alignment step. Average bias over a complete log-slope block is also zero by identification and is not an automatic adequacy criterion. Direct data generation and refitting are supported, but broader GPCM design- planning claims remain outside the current package boundary.

Sparse linked generators are supported through sim_spec or direct assignment = "sparse_linked" plus sparse_controls. Their design-density and rater-link diagnostics are retained in rep_overview; recovery metrics remain parameter-recovery summaries and should not be read as evidence that a sparse linking design is adequate by itself.

The returned ademp component follows the simulation-study framing of Morris, White, and Crowther (2019) and the ADEMP planning/reporting template used in later simulation-study guidance.

Saving and resuming simulations

Pass the same file and analysis arguments on a subsequent call to reuse the completed result without generation or fitting, or to resume an interrupted run. The identity includes generator inputs/specification, fitting controls, requested replications, seed, RNG kind, package R code and native library fingerprints, relevant numerical/diagnostic R options, R/platform, numerical libraries and dependency versions. Changing reps starts a different study; extension of an existing study is not supported. progress and parallel do not change the identity. Cached results retain the settings of their original run.

Recovery runs and serial design evaluations save after every finished trial. Future design evaluations save after a whole design row returns; an interrupted row may need to run again. A partially completed optimizer is not resumed. Fit failures are completed attempts and are saved too; resuming does not redraw failures until they succeed. An unexpected error outside the recorded fit/diagnostic failure routes stops the call and leaves earlier checkpoints available. These files do not change the interpretation or eligibility of the underlying estimates and intervals.

Per-trial seeds are allocated before computation and retained even when seed = NULL; an explicit seed is preferable for reproducing a new run in another file. Each trial controls generation, fitting and diagnostics with its own seed. A matching environment is required for automatic reuse; recorded seeds alone do not guarantee identical floating-point results on other systems. Keep the analysis script and software environment as well.

After completion, readRDS(file) returns the usual result object with an additional reproducibility component containing identity, inputs and trial seeds. Before completion the file is an internal checkpoint; resume through the same public function. Writes use a temporary file in the same directory and checked replacement. A .lock directory prevents concurrent writers. Normal returns/errors release it; after process termination, remove a remaining lock only after checking that no writer is active. Unreadable files are never silently reused or replaced by "on_change".

Monte Carlo uncertainty and missing results

Replications, not parameter rows within a replication, are independent. For a pooled available-row mean, let \(S_r\) be the sum of values in trial \(r\), \(n_r\) its available-row count and \(m = \sum_r S_r / \sum_r n_r\). With \(R\) recorded trials, the ratio-linearization MCSE is $$\mathrm{MCSE}(m) = \frac{\sqrt{R/(R-1)\sum_r(S_r-m n_r)^2}}{\sum_r n_r}.$$ Failed trials contribute zero sums and counts. RMSE uses squared errors and the delta-method factor \(1/(2\sqrt{m})\); McseCoverage95 applies the same ratio calculation to coverage indicators. Fewer than two contributing trials gives NA, as does the RMSE delta MCSE at zero RMSE. These are large-replication approximations; small examples do not qualify performance.

recovery_targets records expected target counts after generation, before fitting. Summaries retain AttemptedReps, FailedReps, ExpectedRows, EstimateRows, SEAvailableRows, CoverageRows and CoverageReps. Coverage95 is conditional on an available interval: report it with CoverageAvailabilityRate and failures. Unavailable intervals are not counted as noncoverage. Availability rates use all expected targets, including failed fits. A generation failure or legacy result can leave the roster unknown; then ExpectedRows and full-denominator availability rates are NA, while KnownTargetRows and KnownTargetReps remain visible.

Interval targets

For non-Person facets, coverage concerns each level minus its facet mean. With \(P = I - 11^T/m\), its covariance is \(P V P^T\); the original marginal SE cannot be reused after alignment. The runner obtains model-based 95\ its numerical/source checks. A complete matched facet roster is required. The row table retains CoverageEstimate, CoverageTruth, SE, Lower95, Upper95, CIEligible and CIReason. RawSE separately preserves the source uncertainty. A valid target SE can remain available when its interval bounds cannot be represented.

JML remains a point-recovery route. Person-score uncertainty is conditional or posterior score uncertainty, not the centered structural interval above. Their coverage is unavailable with an explicit reason; step, slope and population recovery also retain point comparisons without a matching interval implementation here. This does not alter uncertainty available through other model-specific APIs. Numerical eligibility alone does not establish finite-sample coverage or robustness to model misspecification.

Previously saved recovery results

summary(), assess_mfrm_recovery() and summary/coverage plot() routes recompute aggregates from saved rows without fitting. They correct trial MCSEs and withhold old coverage whose centered covariance was not retained. They cannot repair the identified PCM/population truth from old row tables; start a new study to obtain those corrections and matched interval evidence. Read summary(x)$notes and the new availability/reason columns. Directly reading an old x$recovery_summary does not update that stored table. The default file reuse policy rejects the changed implementation identity; use a new file path to preserve the old study.

Typical workflow

  1. Build a simulation specification with build_mfrm_sim_spec() or pass scalar generator arguments directly.

  2. Run simulate_mfrm_recovery(...) with a modest reps value for an initial end-to-end review, then increase reps for stable Monte Carlo summaries.

  3. Inspect summary(x)$recovery_summary and the row-level x$recovery table.

References

Morris, T. P., White, I. R., and Crowther, M. J. (2019). Using simulation studies to evaluate statistical methods. Statistics in Medicine, 38(11), 2074–2102. doi:10.1002/sim.8086 .

See also

simulate_mfrm_data(), evaluate_mfrm_design(), fit_mfrm(), assess_mfrm_recovery(), mfrmr_compatibility_layer

Examples

# Long-running workflow; run explicitly when needed.
# example("simulate_mfrm_recovery", run.dontrun = TRUE)
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
saved <- tempfile(fileext = ".rds")
rec <- simulate_mfrm_recovery(
  n_person = 12,
  n_rater = 2,
  n_criterion = 2,
  reps = 1,
  maxit = 30,
  seed = 123,
  file = saved
)
summary(rec)$recovery_summary[, c("ParameterType", "Facet", "RMSE",
  "McseRMSE", "ExpectedRows", "CoverageRows", "Coverage95")]

# A second identical call reads the result without fitting again.
again <- simulate_mfrm_recovery(n_person = 12, n_rater = 2, n_criterion = 2,
  reps = 1, maxit = 30, seed = 123, file = saved)
identical(rec, again)
unlink(saved)
} # }
